newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus-Schering stock hits high on pill news.
newsitem.headline: Focus-Schering stock hits high on pill news.

text.p: Shares in German drugs company Schering AG hit an all-time high on Wednesday, driven higher by speculation that the Japanese government may soon remove a ban on the oral contraceptive pill.

An hour into the bourse floor session, Schering struck a high of 8.80 marks, or 6.02 percent, at 155 marks after London's Financial Times newspaper said a Japanese government report had declared the pill was safe and effective.
By 1235 GMT the shares were off slightly at 153 marks for a rise of 6.80 marks. The overall DAX index was only slightly higher at 3,235.69 points, up 2.48 points.
Schering is a major manufacturer of oral contraceptives, which have been banned in Japan since their introduction 30 years ago.
The FT said that nine pharmaceutical companies have sought Japanese approval for low-hormone pills and value the market potential at about 100 billion yen ($828 million) a year.
Ronald Koehler, analyst at BHF Bank, said the news of a possible lifting of the ban was good news for Schering, but could be somewhat over-interpreted.

"The headline is a little misleading on the FT article. Only one committee has given its approval and another two have yet to decide, so it does not yet count as approval. It may be optimistic," he said.
"There is not very high acceptance of the pill in Asia -- for example it has a penetration of only three percent in Korea. A cultural revolution in Japan is probably needed."
Markus Rausch at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London said the news from Japan was only one factor boosting the share.
"The sales growth from a possible new marketing opportunity in Japan would in no way justify today's 500 million mark ($299 million) rise in Schering's market capitalisation," said Rausch.

Analysts reckoned that the removal of Japan's ban on the Pill in Japan could generate around 100 million marks turnover for Schering, as the group would be required to manufacture the oral contraceptive with a Japanese partner.
"Set against total turnover of around six billion marks this is not so important," said Rausch.
The fact it would probably take a long time to get permission to produce the Pill also made the news look less exciting than initially thought.
Rausch said that reports on Tuesday that Schering planned to increase turnover by developing its therapeutics and hormone preparation business were having a more positive effect on the share price.
Analysts cited reports that the group planned to increase sales by 850 million marks through new products in the next three years.
"Up until now the market thought that Schering had no new products in the pipeline," said Rausch.
